rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.5-2.8 and 3 - the authors run their own WEAP and AquaCrop model simulations for the Chichaoua-Mejjate basin under five RCMs and ten management/climate scenarios to 2050, and report their own projected net precipitation, crop water demand, unmet demand and aquifer balance results.
rows.notes: The study is a primary modelling study, but its only evidence on drip is Scenario 2 (Sections 2.8.4 and 3.5), a WEAP projection in which drip is adopted on 50% of the PMH gravity perimeters together with concreting 70% of earth canals; the simulated effect (annual water demand down ~4%, unmet demand reduced by 41%/39% under RCP4.5/8.5, shortage in Douirane cut by 73-74%) comes from an assumed plot efficiency of 95% for drip taken from Le Page et al. 2020 (Table 3) and is never compared with measured water use or savings in the real system. Drip is also not isolated from the canal-lining measure. AquaCrop calibration against Agriculture Department crop water demand concerns baseline crop needs, not the drip effect. Hence the model run does not qualify as own evidence on drip water conservation under the rules. The paper does report dispersion-like ranges only for climate/net precipitation, not for the drip scenario, and states no limitations specific to the drip result beyond generic further-research remarks.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Study is a WEAP/AquaCrop decision-support modelling exercise under RCP4.5/8.5; drip irrigation appears only as an assumed efficiency parameter (95% plot efficiency) in a scenario, with no field measurement or validation of drip water savings.
